how: A participant proposes painting Tux and receives a coordination response without acquiring demonstrated command over the later shared project.
Participants recruit hands to start and finish the Linux pictures.
The proposed picture gives another participant a concrete project to answer with a coordination request.
Calls and later image reports do not identify builders recruited by those calls.
An all-day repairer doubts whether the available effort can keep the image standing.
A learner thanks an explainer without requesting another action.
A direct refusal can be a bare No rather than the reason-giving refusal predicted by the answer-preference mechanism.
Prospective contributors need explanations of the event before they can understand how to participate.
Supplying a target must sometimes be supplemented by teaching color selection, placement controls and login.
Participants identify neighboring pictures without negotiating or acting on those neighbors.
Participants negotiate templates, colors, GNU additions, punctuation and possible embellishments.
Participants display the Linux work and report its completion.
Contributors circulate the current design and ask placers to follow the same image.
Revised targets require renewed visibility among defenders who otherwise erase intended changes.
Posting a revised design does not settle it when teammates continue repairing toward an older target.
Organizing relays targets and requests between the local thread, a kindred subreddit and chat without exposing all external decisions.
The external coordination relay prevents inferring absent organization and one room cannot test the cross-room frequency claim.
Participants propose automation, report making tools and consider account rules without establishing every tool's operation.
Participants dispute fairness, creative effort and whether guide-following humans can resemble bots.
A conditional offer of outside maintenance does not establish contact, acceptance or delivered automated placements.
Strain explains a later script request but cannot explain all tool planning or establish subsequent deployment.
Participants repair damage, rally defenders and report continuous watching with rapid fixes.
Participants propose a harder-to-vandalize separator and explain the slash as a concession to repeated swastika edits.
A completion report is answered by the need to defend the finished image.
Participants explain visible tile attribution and separately express uncertainty about which community made the whole picture.
Attribution includes acknowledging friendly mistakes and listing suspected automated placers without verifying the suspicion.
Participants report a letters-protection agreement and negotiate prospective overlap without showing final settlement of every proposal.
A visitor speaks for a neighboring project while seeking a treaty and explaining proposed overlap.
Anticipated overlap can prompt a preemptive treaty request before a demonstrated war or erosion.
The prospective-overlap exchange does not establish erosion as the cause of negotiation.
Participants defend neighbors' rightful space, appeal for restraint and exchange an apology for accidental damage.
The stated reason for sparing the Lost work is its rightful maintenance rather than an identified settled border.
Participants greet neighbors, report outside assistance and describe helping another community's picture.
A visitor reports cleaning other vandalism after an apology was accepted and their accidental pixel had been repaired.
A maintenance offer following reports of repair establishes offered help but not acceptance or delivered assistance.
Apology and helpful repair do not demonstrate help traded through a negotiated border channel.
Coordination referrals and a maintenance offer do not establish a coalition or mutual-defense commitment.
Reports of strain and outside coordination do not expose a transition into coalition membership.
A restart can correct an initially misplaced drawing rather than follow erasure or defeat.
The cited restart concerns initial placement error and does not show relocation after loss.
Doubt about sustaining repair is not connected to a decision to abandon and move.
Protecting another group's letters does not establish a host governing guest work.
Teammate erasure disputes a visible design target rather than anyone's authority to bind placers to treaties.
The cited agreement and treaty request have no visible answer contesting who may bind the room.
Recognizing the community symbol prompts a nonsubscriber to identify with its people and report joining defense.
A reply playfully redescribes human watchers as a botnet without establishing actual automation or inherited lore.
The named Windows target does not establish a prior tie naming the rival within the attack turn.
The hostile Windows exchange supplies no account of an earlier quarrel carried into the canvas.
Participants post Linux-themed April Fools claims and recognize, decode or object to them.
Moderators remove satire and a coordination-script post while a poster anticipates the no-memes rule.
An off-topic removal supplies no evidence that a flood of recruiting calls caused the moderation response.
Participants show the work, congratulate its makers and announce completed Linux pictures.
A participant marks personal contribution by reporting work done one pixel at a time.
Displaying the completed work gives participants an object for praise and credit.
Participants present the final form and lament the eye's surviving red dot after closure.
A participant records their experience of watching factions fight through timelapses rather than joining those fights.
A participant reports deterioration of a previously perfect picture without claiming to repair it.
A participant shares an outside timeline of the logo without establishing a preservation campaign.
Celebration and a later timeline occur without evidence that the celebration prompted recording.
The red-dot lament does not show a request to clean a shared copy or a dispute over which version to preserve.
The final image and red-dot complaint do not show a decision to continue the effort beyond the event.
Recording a final image is not visibly connected to a plan for carrying the effort forward.
A request to deface a named logo receives a report of trying to convert its lettering.
An individual reports trying and failing to remove GNU rather than contributing to shared design consensus.
A post-close imagined griefing program is attack talk rather than evidence of a deployed program.
An individual asks another to stop changing the leaf and defends it as art without speaking for the Linux project.
A call to cleanse follows the individual defense of the leaf without establishing a room-adopted campaign.
An individual announces bot writing for an erasure project without showing operation or a Linux-room mandate.
The Windows attack exchange does not identify its participants as hands recruited by the earlier Tux calls.
The cited Windows attack exchange contains no refusal or appeal for restraint answering that attack.
The cited Windows attack exchange contains no invocation of a truce or alternative deal.
Post-close blame and imagined griefing do not identify a reciprocal contest with a rival room.
The attack exchanges do not show a subsequent room-level contest with an identified rival.
